title: Session of Crossroads Community Church and RE Mark Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: In consolidated cases 2008-01 and 2008-10, the SJC answered both alleged errors negatively, affirmed Presbytery’s licensing and ordination actions, and denied both complaints. No further proceedings or relief were ordered.
first_summary: Two consolidated complaints challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s licensing and ordination of a candidate who believed Scripture could permit women to hold the deacon’s office but promised to follow the BCO and not ordain women. The SJC denied both complaints and affirmed Presbytery, distinguishing subscription to doctrinal standards from approval of BCO practices and deferring to Presbytery’s judgment that the candidate could credibly affirm his ordination vow.
summary: Two consolidated complaints challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s licensing and ordination of a candidate who believed Scripture could permit women to hold the deacon’s office but promised to follow the BCO and not ordain women. The SJC denied both complaints and affirmed Presbytery. It distinguished subscription to doctrinal standards from approval of BCO practices, applied a three-part inquiry, and deferred to Presbytery on the candidate’s credible vow. Because complainants identified no violated doctrinal standard, no error was shown. The ruling reaffirmed that the BCO bars ordaining women as deacons.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The consolidated caption appears at lines 13–14; the majority judgment and reasoning appear at lines 96–228, followed by separately labeled concurrence and dissent.
evidence_notes.dispute: The issues were whether Presbytery erred in licensing and ordaining a candidate with a stated BCO difference concerning women and the deacon’s office despite his promised conformity; printed p. 179, lines 73–94.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Both issues were answered “No” at lines 96–99. The three-part inquiry appears at lines 147–151, its application at lines 185–224, and affirmance and denial at line 228.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The majority expressly held that the BCO prohibits ordaining women as deacons and noted that later nonconforming conduct could prompt action; printed pp. 183–186, lines 159–177 and 224–226. The contrary view at lines 288–350 is dissent.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference. Presbytery’s committee merely noted a 1984 case; printed p. 178, lines 49–51.
